problem: The sentence 'A smooth curve has a continuous derivative, so it has no sharp corner' is not reliable. A curve whose derivative is continuous can still vanish at a point and have a cusp, for example the astroid x=cos³t, y=sin³t. Under the chapter's own definition such a curve counts as smooth, yet it has sharp points.
fix: Say instead: 'Here smooth means f′ is continuous on [a,b]. The formula needs the derivative to exist everywhere on the interval; at a corner, where the derivative fails, split the curve and add the pieces.'

problem: 'dx, dy, dt and L must use one consistent length unit' is wrong when the parameter t is not a length (for example t is time in seconds). Then dt has the unit of the parameter, and the length comes out right because dx/dt has units of length per unit t.
fix: Say: 'Keep one length unit for x, y and L. The parameter t keeps its own unit; dx/dt and dy/dt then carry length per unit t, so the product with dt gives length.'

problem: The answer says area adds rectangle heights giving f(x)Δx. For a curve below the x-axis f is negative, and the area between the curve and the x-axis is built from |f(x)|Δx, not f(x)Δx.
fix: Say: 'Area between the curve and the x-axis adds heights |f(x)|, giving |f(x)|Δx; arc length adds chord lengths √(Δx²+Δy²).'
